item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
item.description:
World
Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
November 26, 20268:47 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Relatives and healthcare workers prepare to bury a victim of Ebola, in Beni, North Kivu province, Congo, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026.
Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP
BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Thursday, as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half the 12,021 people confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo's Ministry of Health. It is also the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.
The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.

item.description:

North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
November 26, 20268:31 AM ET
By

In this photo provided by the North Korean government, leader Kim Jong Un inspects a facility the government says is for producing weapons-grade nuclear material at an undisclosed location in North Korea, Monday, Nov. 25, 2026.
Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP

Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP
SEOUL, South Korea — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.
Experts say Kim likely wants to show off his evolving nuclear arsenal, the backbone of his authoritarian rule, and reaffirm his rejection of any future talks on dismantling his nuclear program.
The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
November 26, 20261:53 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
FILE - Elon Musk listens as President Donald Trump speaks during an event at the U.S. Institute of Peace, Oct. 8, 2026, in Washington.
Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP
The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.
Big tech's next move is to put data centers in space. Can it work?
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX's one million "orbital compute modules" (forming a data center constellation called "Starmind") would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing "the full power of the sun."

item.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
item.description:
Obituaries
Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
November 26, 20261:34 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
FILE - Music group Duran Duran poses at The Sony Club in New York, Oct. 12, 2004. From left are John Taylor, Nick Rhodes, Roger Taylor, Simon Le Bon and Andy Taylor.
Jim Cooper/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Jim Cooper/AP
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.
"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed," the band said.
